rationale: Independently inspected all 50 selected additions across 28 boards and verified each exact candidate ID, pair, output and candidate hash is a subset of my original semantic accepts. No rejected or A5-held recipe is included. Independently rebuilt all 80 live books from the proposed catalog and obtained byte-identical live-audit.json; all nine bound runtime source hashes match. Existing seeds, target, core pairs/results, stored core routes, projected concept counts, exact par and target-ID privacy remain intact. The extension adds 33 productive openings and 17 final target pairs, restoring concrete equivalent monastery/club/story classes and distinctive cultural or geographical connections without inventing new concepts or opening the broad graph. Pair/concept/result bounds and exact graph/node metadata guards are present. I checked score arithmetic: empty trials do not reduce score, successful crafts beyond par still cost 120, hints cost 150 and the 100-point floor remains. This improves consistency and removes the score penalty for experimentation within existing target challenges. It does not establish open-ended crafting, new side discoveries or player acceptance: 12 boards still have one opening, 19 still have one final target pair, and only 223 of 1226 total seed pairs are productive. These limitations must remain explicit rather than presenting the batch as a complete freedom/content redesign.
